piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:32, Op.20 No.2
piece.why: Cello leads in its tenor register above Violin II and viola while Violin I is silent, then Violin I takes over, then Violin II (doubled by viola) carries the line under a Violin I pedal.

roster.label: Church brass: 2 trumpets (one beginner), horn, euphonium

plan.summary: The horn plays the cello's opening tune and the euphonium plays the bass all the way through. Trumpet 2 (beginner) plays the simple Violin 2 accompaniment. When Violin 1 brings the motif back high at bar 6, Trumpet 1 takes it an octave lower and carries the tune to the end, switching to Violin 2's falling scale for the closing phrase. The horn moves to the harmony line in thirds and then the viola's inner line. The euphonium keeps the bass going at bar 12, where the viola is the lowest line, then moves to the cello's G pedal. Trumpet 2 ends on the G pedal.

assignments.reason: The cello's opening tune (G3–G4) fits the horn as written, and the horn's warm tone suits this singing line.
Simple Violin 2 accompaniment in the beginner's comfortable B3–E4 range. Play softly under the horn.
This accompaniment phrase dips to G3, below Trumpet 2's range, so Trumpet 1 covers it before taking the tune.
Trumpet 2 comes back for the end of the accompaniment phrase, which is back in its easy range.
Here the viola carries the bass (arpeggios and repeated Cs), and it fits the euphonium as written.
Same bass line, an octave down (G2–G3), so it stays under the trumpet tune and the horn harmony. Bar 12 is included because the viola is still the lowest line there (G2–E4 after the shift).
The cello's low G pedal is the real bass at the end and sits comfortably on euphonium.
Violin 1 brings the opening motif back high and takes over the melody. An octave down (D4–D5) it fits trumpet, and its bright tone carries the climax.
The tune moves to Violin 2's falling scale. Bar 12 reaches G5, so Trumpet 1 plays this bar an octave down.
The rest of the closing scale sits in Trumpet 1's range as written.
Violin 2's harmony in thirds, taken two octaves down so the high D6s fit the horn and it sits under the trumpet tune.
The line drops to A4/B4 here, so the horn moves up to one octave down to stay in range. The phrase changes at this point anyway.
The viola's inner line runs parallel to the closing melody. It is smooth and fits the horn as written.
Easy G4 pedal for the beginner. It has the same notes and rhythm as Violin 1's held G, taken from the cello so every note fits.

dropped.reason: Violin 2 jumps up to G5–F♯5, apparently doubling Violin 1's tune. That is above Trumpet 2's range, and Trumpet 1 already plays the tune.
Violin 1's G pedal is the same as the cello's pedal (same notes and rhythm), which Trumpet 2 plays at G4. The low final Gs were out of Trumpet 2's range.
